name: sbml-decomposition
title: SBML in Tellurium vs process-bigraph decomposition — speed × accuracy × composability, and the limits of SBML itself
lead: A methods investigation, not a biology result. Seven studies run SBML models — and, at the edges, a scaled multi-organ body and a stochastic agent-based model — across a spectrum of implementations (on a small set of generic composites) under one workspace, each measured on speed, accuracy, and composability. The deliverable is a decision guide: which decomposition patterns to use, which to avoid, where Tellurium strains, and where SBML stops applying.

at_a_glance.role: monolithic SBML in libroadrunner/CVODE — the speed + accuracy reference (bulk-port binding, ~12% faster, bit-identical)
same model split mechanically into two reaction groups on one additive store — isolates orchestration overhead + split error (shrinks with the coupling interval; strong-coupling seam diverges)
biological upper/lower seam as two coupled process nodes sharing a store — genuine composability (0.468->0.100 as the step shrinks)
fully native process-bigraph RHS, no libroadrunner — ~1e-7 fidelity; scalar vs array leaf irrelevant at 17 species
cross-engine hybrid (Tellurium + COPASI / native at one seam) — engines are interchangeable, a composition a monolith cannot express
ensembles of monoliths: same-rate on Ray (7.5x wall-clock win) and multi-rate on process-bigraph #270's heap scheduler (bit-identical to scan; advantage grows with process count)
ADVERSARIAL: scale a model until Tellurium strains (monolithic BUILD ~O(N^1.6); decomposition is not a free win) and ask whether an ABM can be SBML (only in the large-population limit)

how_to_read: Start with sbml-in-tellurium (the reference), read mechanical-split-cost -> biological-modular-seam -> fully-native-pbg as increasing decomposition (accuracy falls, composability rises), then cross-engine-coupling (the capability proof) and ensemble-and-multirate (the parallel and scheduler wins). bigger-models-and-abm-limit holds the two boundary probes: where the monolith strains at scale and where SBML stops applying (the adversarial case). The 3-way tradeoff map and the decision table are the deliverable.

glossary.definition: advancing subsets of a system separately over an interval then composing — introduces a splitting error that shrinks with the interval
framework time / total wall-clock from Composite.timing_summary(); the SHARE of time outside process invoke(), largest for cheap processes — NOT the decomposition cost
the ability to substitute a submodel, couple through a shared store, mix engines, or wire across scales — what decomposition buys
the deterministic large-population ODE limit of a stochastic agent-based model; valid only when discreteness, stochasticity and extinction are negligible

question: When you have a biochemical model, when should you run it monolithically in Tellurium (libroadrunner/CVODE) and when is it worth decomposing it into vivarium / process-bigraph sub-processes — and what does each point on that spectrum cost in performance and accuracy, buy in composability, and where does Tellurium (and SBML itself) stop being the right tool as models get larger or stop being reaction networks at all?
hypothesis: Across the spectrum monolithic Tellurium → split → modular → fully-native process-bigraph, performance and accuracy degrade monotonically while composability rises, so no point dominates. Beyond the single-model comparison we predict two boundaries: (a) the monolithic libroadrunner build strains superlinearly as models scale, so decomposition's modularity matters at size even though it is not free on wall-clock; and (b) not every model is expressible as SBML — an agent-based model reduces to an SBML/ODE only in the large-population, well-mixed, deterministic limit.

executive.what_is_this: A head-to-head of ways to run the same model — from a single libroadrunner/CVODE call to a fully hand-written process-bigraph network — plus two boundary probes: scaling a model until Tellurium's build strains, and asking whether an agent-based model can even be an SBML model. Seven member studies, measured on speed × accuracy × composability.
executive.verdict: No single implementation wins on all axes. Monolithic Tellurium is the fastest implementation and the numerical reference; every decomposition adds orchestration overhead and additive-split (Jacobi) coupling error that shrinks as the coupling interval shrinks. The payoff is strictly composability: only the decomposed studies can substitute a submodel, couple through a store, or mix engines (cross-engine-coupling runs half libroadrunner / half a second engine in one composite — impossible for a monolith — and the engines are interchangeable at the seam). The ensemble study is the one place vivarium wins on wall-clock (7.5× via Ray). Two boundaries sharpen the picture: as a model scales, the monolithic libroadrunner BUILD time strains superlinearly (~O(N^1.6)) — but decomposition is not a free win (it is slower end-to-end at every size we measured, paying off only at very large models, and with accuracy degradation); and an ABM reduces to an SBML/Tellurium ODE only in the large-population limit — at small populations the ODE misses the stochastic collapse entirely (predators go extinct in 86.5% of runs; the ODE cycles forever).

decisions_needed.question: Adopt the opt-in bulk-binding + heap scheduler across all tellurium studies and re-measure?
decisions_needed.context: viva-tellurium bulk_species (#24) gives sbml-in-tellurium ~12% bit-identical; process-bigraph #270's heap scheduler helps mismatched-interval composites. Both are merged; sbml-in-tellurium already uses bulk.

scientific_argument.main_claim: On the implementation spectrum, speed and accuracy are best at the monolithic pole and composability at the decomposed pole — a genuine tradeoff with no dominating point — and the tool itself has limits: Tellurium's monolithic build strains superlinearly at scale, and SBML cannot represent an agent-based model outside its mean-field limit.
evidence_for: sbml-in-tellurium (monolithic) matches direct libroadrunner to ~1e-6 and is the fastest implementation; bulk-port binding makes it ~12% faster, bit-identical.

mechanical-split-cost and biological-modular-seam show real split error that shrinks with the coupling interval (mechanical-split-cost, additive Jacobi coupling: 0.857 at 0.1 -> 0.112 at 0.0125 -> 0.0066 at 0.001; biological-modular-seam: 0.468 -> 0.100). The additive coupling converges but is not free: at 0.0125 it is 0.112.
fully-native-pbg (fully native) reaches ~1e-7 fidelity with no libroadrunner at runtime; at 17 species the scalar-dict vs numpy-array leaf choice is perf-irrelevant.

cross-engine-coupling runs a cross-engine hybrid (libroadrunner + a second engine in one composite) that a monolith cannot express, with either the native or the COPASI lower half matching the Tellurium lower half at the same interval to ~3e-7 (an engine-swap drop-in, not bit-reproducible) — the composability payoff.
ensemble-and-multirate (same-rate ensemble) achieves a real 7.5x wall-clock speedup via Ray.

ensemble-and-multirate (multi-rate ensemble) shows process-bigraph #270's heap scheduler is bit-identical to the scan loop and its multi-rate advantage grows with process count (1.0x->1.64x over P=4->256).
bigger-models-and-abm-limit measures the monolithic libroadrunner BUILD straining superlinearly (~O(N^1.64), 0.20s->18.5s over 97->1537 species).
bigger-models-and-abm-limit shows the ABM->SBML mean-field reduction is valid at large population (K=400: 4.9% error, no extinction).
evidence_against: overhead_fraction (framework SHARE of wall-clock) is HIGHEST for the cheap monolith (~0.32) and lowest for decomposed/native studies — a cheap process makes the framework look expensive, so share is NOT the decomposition cost.

Decomposition is slower END-TO-END than the monolith at every multi-organ size measured (bigger-models-and-abm-limit); it only build-wins at ~769+ species, and its accuracy degrades at scale (0.31 at 385 species).
A clean mechanical split (mechanical-split-cost) was only possible across a weakly-coupled seam; splitting across the strong energy coupling diverges.
At small population the ABM→SBML reduction is INVALID (bigger-models-and-abm-limit, K=8): the ODE misses the stochastic collapse the ABM shows (predator extinction 86.5%, total 51%).
key_figures: bigger-models-and-abm-limit multi-organ strain curve (build + run vs species count)
bigger-models-and-abm-limit ABM vs mean-field ODE (large pop match, small pop collapse)
caveats: Core comparison is one metabolic model (Teusink glycolysis); bigger-models-and-abm-limit holds the boundary probes with their own synthetic/biological vehicles.
Mismatched coupling intervals carry an O(P²) scheduler cost in pb ≤1.10.x; process-bigraph #270 (merged) reduces it to ~O(P log P). Prefer equal intervals on older pins.
bigger-models-and-abm-limit: the decomposed multi-organ run at very large N (≥256 species) was left unmeasured; no end-to-end scale win is claimed there.
bigger-models-and-abm-limit: ABM extinction fractions are parameter- and scale-specific; the qualitative limit (ODE shows zero extinction) is general.

competing_frameworks.name: monolith-always
competing_frameworks.prediction: running the whole model in Tellurium is always the right choice
competing_frameworks.discriminated_by: cross-engine-coupling (a cross-engine composition the monolith cannot express), ensemble-and-multirate (the ensemble wall-clock win), and bigger-models-and-abm-limit (the monolithic build strain at scale)

competing_frameworks.name: decompose-always
competing_frameworks.prediction: process-bigraph decomposition is free / always worth it
competing_frameworks.discriminated_by: mechanical-split-cost, biological-modular-seam, fully-native-pbg + bigger-models-and-abm-limit — the measured, non-zero speed + accuracy cost of every decomposition, slower end-to-end at every size measured

competing_frameworks.name: everything-is-SBML
competing_frameworks.prediction: any dynamical model can be captured as an SBML/Tellurium model
competing_frameworks.discriminated_by: bigger-models-and-abm-limit — an ABM reduces to SBML only in the large-population limit; at small populations the ODE structurally misses stochastic extinction

studies.name: sbml-in-tellurium
studies.title: Monolithic Tellurium (reference)
studies.question: Does the whole SBML model, integrated in one libroadrunner/CVODE call through a single TelluriumProcess, reproduce the model's reference trajectory, and what is its performance baseline?
methods: one engine process over the whole model (tellurium | copasi | native)

findings.summary: Matches direct libroadrunner to max_rel_err ~1e-6 on a shared grid (rtol 1e-6, atol 1e-9).

overhead_fraction ~0.32 (highest of all studies): the single CVODE call is so cheap that framework time dominates its share — framework SHARE is largest for the cheapest process, not the most decomposed.

Bulk-port binding (viva-tellurium bulk_species + Array species leaf, libroadrunner bulk C API) makes sbml-in-tellurium ~12% faster wall-clock, BIT-IDENTICAL (max abs trajectory diff 0.0). The win lands in total runtime, not overhead_fraction (which stays ~0.32) — a real speedup that doesn't move the framework SHARE, reinforcing that share != cost.

studies.claim: Monolithic Tellurium reproduces the reference to ~1e-6 and is the fastest approach — the speed + accuracy reference.

derived.insight: Matches direct libroadrunner to max_rel_err ~1e-6 on a shared grid (rtol 1e-6, atol 1e-9).

studies.name: mechanical-split-cost
studies.title: Mechanical split: the cost of splitting
studies.question: If the same model is split mechanically (not along a biological seam) into two reaction groups that exchange state through ONE shared additive store each coupling interval, how much orchestration overhead and splitting error does that add, and does the error shrink with the interval?
methods: two engine nodes over one additive species store (Jacobi split)

findings.summary: Measured on the additive (Jacobi) reaction_split(seam=mechanical) composite against the monolithic Tellurium reference, max_rel_err by coupling interval: 0.1 → 0.857; 0.05 (composite default) → 0.851; 0.025 → 0.277; 0.0125 → 0.112; 0.005 → 0.037; 0.001 → 0.0066; 0.0005 → 0.0033. The error shrinks monotonically with the interval. Additive coupling does NOT reach the earlier provisional 0.10 bound at 0.0125 (0.112); it gets under 0.15 there and under 0.05 by 0.005. Tolerance T=0.15 at the fine interval.
AVOID generalizing: a clean split only worked across the weak glycogen/trehalose sinks. Splitting across the strong energy (P/ATP/ADP, sqrt adenylate rule) coupling diverges for all intervals.

Method note: the generic reaction_split(seam=mechanical) composite couples additively (Jacobi: both reaction groups advance from the same state and their deltas sum), not by a sequential Lie split. This is a methods finding: additive coupling converges to the monolith as the interval shrinks but pays more error at a given interval than a sequential split would.

studies.claim: Mechanical-split (additive-coupling) error is real and shrinks monotonically with the coupling interval (max relative error 0.857 at 0.1 → 0.112 at 0.0125 → 0.0066 at 0.001, measured against the monolithic reference); a clean split was only possible across the weakly-coupled glycogen/trehalose sinks — splitting across the strong P/ATP/ADP energy coupling diverges.

derived.insight: Measured on the additive (Jacobi) reaction_split(seam=mechanical) composite against the monolithic Tellurium reference, max_rel_err by coupling interval: 0.1 → 0.857; 0.05 (composite default) → 0.851; 0.025 → 0.277; 0.0125 → 0.112; 0.005 → 0.037; 0.001 → 0.0066; 0.0005 → 0.0033. The error shrinks monotonically with the interval. Additive coupling does NOT reach the earlier provisional 0.10 bound at 0.0125 (0.112); it gets under 0.15 there and under 0.05 by 0.005. Tolerance T=0.15 at the fine interval.

studies.name: biological-modular-seam
studies.title: Biological seam: modular submodels
studies.question: If the model is partitioned along a biological seam (upper vs lower glycolysis at aldolase/F16P) into two coupled process nodes sharing a store, does it still reproduce the reference, and is this a genuine multi-process composition?
methods: two engine nodes over one additive species store (Jacobi split)

findings.summary: Two process nodes share one species store, reconciling additively through the bigraph apply path (verified: core.apply/reconcile sum the deltas, not a local loop). Reproduces the mechanical-split reference exactly.
coupling step 0.002 → max_rel_err 0.468; 0.0005 → 0.100 (T=0.15). Looser than mechanical-split-cost because this seam crosses the strong energy coupling; divergence is guarded to status=diverged.
overhead_fraction ~0.05 (far below the monolith's 0.32): the decomposed composite spends more wall-clock inside the processes, so the framework is a smaller share.

studies.claim: A biological-seam decomposition reproduces the reference (0.468 → 0.100 as the coupling step shrinks, T=0.15) as a GENUINE multi-process composition — the first point on the spectrum where the model is composable.

derived.insight: Two process nodes share one species store, reconciling additively through the bigraph apply path (verified: core.apply/reconcile sum the deltas, not a local loop). Reproduces the mechanical-split reference exactly.

studies.name: fully-native-pbg
studies.title: Fully native process-bigraph
studies.question: Can the glycolysis ODE network be reimplemented as native process-bigraph processes (no libroadrunner at runtime) at reference fidelity, and does the state leaf representation (scalar-dict vs numpy-array) matter for performance at this scale?

findings.summary: Native RHS (all 17 reactions + 3 sqrt adenylate rules) matches the reference to max_rel_err ~1.05e-7; scalar and array variants bitwise identical.

Scalar-dict vs numpy-array overhead_fraction indistinguishable (0.023 vs 0.022); per-process leaf-crossing ~6.8ms vs 6.7ms, swamped by the ~289ms LSODA integration. The scalar-dict framework tax is linear in element count and only matters at large state.

studies.claim: A fully native process-bigraph implementation reaches reference fidelity (~1e-7); at 17 species the scalar-dict-vs-array leaf choice is perf-irrelevant (only bites at 100s-1000s of species).

derived.insight: Native RHS (all 17 reactions + 3 sqrt adenylate rules) matches the reference to max_rel_err ~1.05e-7; scalar and array variants bitwise identical.

studies.name: cross-engine-coupling
studies.title: Cross-engine coupling: engines are interchangeable at a seam
studies.question: Can one composite run part of the model in one engine and part in another (libroadrunner, COPASI, or the native process), sharing one store - a composition a monolithic SBML model structurally cannot express - and are the engines interchangeable at the seam?
methods: two engine nodes over one additive species store (Jacobi split)

findings.summary: Hybrid composite: upper glycolysis (Tellurium SubmodelProcess) + lower glycolysis (NativeSubmodelProcess) share one species store, reconciling additively — a composition a single libroadrunner model cannot express.

Matches the Tellurium+Tellurium reference at the same interval (0.005) when the lower half is swapped (same ODEs, different engine): max_rel_err 3.19e-7 for the COPASI swap, 3.20e-7 for the native swap; the monolith-impossibility is STRUCTURAL, not numeric. Accuracy-exempt in the 3-way figure.

Engine interchangeability is measured on both swaps (seam=aldolase, interval 0.005, vs tellurium+tellurium): tellurium+COPASI 3.19e-7, tellurium+native 3.20e-7. Both are ~1e-7 engine-swap drop-ins; COPASI is not bit-reproducible and varies at the ~1e-7 level run to run.

studies.claim: A single composite runs HALF in one engine and HALF in another, sharing one store - structurally impossible for a monolith. Swapping the lower half of the seam=aldolase composite from Tellurium to COPASI or to the native process reproduces the Tellurium+Tellurium trajectory at the same coupling interval (0.005) to max relative error 3.2e-7 (COPASI 3.19e-7, native 3.20e-7, measured); the engines are interchangeable at a seam as a ~1e-7 drop-in (COPASI is not bit-reproducible run to run). This is the composability payoff, not a numeric result.

derived.insight: Hybrid composite: upper glycolysis (Tellurium SubmodelProcess) + lower glycolysis (NativeSubmodelProcess) share one species store, reconciling additively — a composition a single libroadrunner model cannot express.

studies.name: ensemble-and-multirate
studies.title: Ensemble throughput and multi-rate scheduling
studies.question: When many instances of the monolithic model are run together, (a) as a same-rate parameter ensemble does vivarium orchestration on a real parallel backend (Ray) deliver a genuine throughput speedup, and (b) as a genuinely multi-rate ensemble (each instance on a different interval) does process-bigraph #270's event-heap scheduler beat the stock scan loop as the process count grows, while staying bit-identical?
methods: multi-rate: geometric per-instance intervals, #270 heap scheduler

findings.summary: [same-rate/Ray] n_instances=8, 16 CPUs: serial 1.189s → Ray 0.158s = 7.52x real speedup (backend=ray, speedup_claimed=true).

[same-rate/Ray] libroadrunner does NOT release the GIL during .simulate() (8-instance ThreadPool = 0.99x), so Ray's separate OS processes are the only path; in-process parallel_processes backfires for this CVODE-wrapping work.

[multi-rate/heap] Scan and heap are bit-identical at every measured P — multirate_scaling records a per-N bit_identical flag (np.array_equal of the two schedulers' final state across every instance store), True at each of P=4..256, and a dedicated test asserts it across the measured Ns (not just the small-N case). #270 changes only the order in which due processes are popped, never the math. The multi-rate composite is uncoupled (independent monoliths, empty inputs), so there is no split-coupling divergence to confound the timing.

[multi-rate/heap] Measured scan vs heap run() wall-clock (median of 3, construction excluded), geometric intervals i_fast=H/(3P)..i_slow=3H, H=20: P=4 scan=0.0082s heap=0.0083s (0.98x); P=16 0.0468s / 0.0492s (0.95x); P=64 0.419s / 0.371s (1.13x); P=128 1.555s / 1.280s (1.22x); P=256 6.598s / 4.019s (1.64x). The heap/scan speedup rises monotonically with P and crosses over near P~50-64.

[multi-rate/heap] Honesty: heap is ~5% SLOWER at tiny P (P=4,16) — the event-heap bookkeeping has nothing to gain when the per-tick scan is trivially short — exactly #270's documented single-rate penalty. The win is modest (<=1.64x) at the P a test can afford because the real libroadrunner/CVODE update per due process dominates the per-tick Python scan at small P (measured crossover ~P=50-64). #270's cheap-process micro-benchmark (where the scheduler is the whole cost) is 4.8x@P=100 rising to 46x@P=1000; ensemble-and-multirate reproduces the TREND with real integrator instances, not those multipliers.

[multi-rate/heap] Scheduler API used (#270): the strategy is the "scheduler" CONFIG FIELD on the Composite (Composite({"state": doc, "scheduler": "heap"|"scan"|"auto"}, core=core)); "auto" (the default) picks heap only when more than one distinct process interval is present. ensemble-and-multirate selects "scan" vs "heap" explicitly to measure both.

studies.claim: A Ray ensemble of monoliths gives a real 7.5x wall-clock speedup on 16 cores — the one study where vivarium wins on speed; libroadrunner does NOT release the GIL, so in-process threads cannot (they backfire). Separately, process-bigraph #270's event-heap scheduler is bit-identical to the stock scan loop (same math, different tick order) and its wall-clock advantage grows monotonically with P on a genuinely multi-rate composite — measured 0.98x at P=4 (heap bookkeeping with nothing to gain), crossing over near P~50-64, to 1.64x at P=256 on real libroadrunner/CVODE instances. The per-process CVODE integration dominates the per-tick scan until P reaches the low hundreds, so the multiplier is modest at the P a unit test can afford; it is reported as measured, and the regime where it grows large (hundreds-to-thousands of cheap processes) is #270's own 4.8x@P=100 -> 46x@P=1000 micro-benchmark, cited not reproduced.

derived.insight: [same-rate/Ray] n_instances=8, 16 CPUs: serial 1.189s → Ray 0.158s = 7.52x real speedup (backend=ray, speedup_claimed=true).

studies.name: bigger-models-and-abm-limit
studies.title: Bigger models and the ABM limit (adversarial)
studies.question: Where do the SBML/Tellurium assumptions stop holding: (a) as an SBML model grows to hundreds-to-thousands of species, where does a monolithic libroadrunner/CVODE instance strain, and does decomposing it come out ahead end-to-end; (b) can an agent-based model even BE an SBML/Tellurium model, and where does its mean-field ODE reduction hold and structurally break?
methods: one engine process over the whole model (tellurium | copasi | native)

findings.summary: [scale] STRONG RESULT — the monolithic libroadrunner BUILD (compile) strains superlinearly: measured medians 0.20 s at 97 species, 1.76 s at 385, 5.54 s at 769, 18.5 s at 1537 species — ~94x the build cost for ~16x the reactions (~O(N^1.64)). The dense-CVODE integration blows up alongside it (0.0023 s -> 0.058 s -> 0.395 s -> 2.56 s). Both halves of the monolithic cost grow superlinearly; this is the real, well-measured strain point and this study's headline.

[scale] HONEST NEGATIVE — decomposition does NOT build "several-fold faster by hundreds of species". The decomposed build is N separate libroadrunner setups: SLOWER than the single monolithic compile up to ~100 species (97 sp: 0.34 s vs 0.20 s, 1.7x slower), roughly at PARITY by 385 species (1.40 vs 1.76 s), and a clear win only at ~1500 species (7.75 vs 18.5 s, 2.4x). The build crossover is at the hundreds-of-species scale, not before.

[scale] HONEST NEGATIVE (end-to-end) — the decomposed per-tick RUN overhead dwarfs the monolith's raw CVODE run: at 385 species decomp_run 0.95 s vs mono_run 0.058 s (~16x). So the decomposed body is SLOWER END-TO-END at every N measured: mono_total vs decomp_total = 0.017 vs 0.044 s (N=2), 0.039 vs 0.143 (N=8), 0.200 vs 0.559 (N=32), 1.81 vs 2.35 (N=128). The end-to-end gap narrows as N grows (3.6x -> 1.3x), but the decomposed run is UNMEASURED past N=128 (too slow for the harness), so NO end-to-end crossover is claimed. Decomposition trades the monolith's superlinear build for higher run overhead; it would only pay off end-to-end on models larger than we measured.

[scale] The coupling is genuine: Glc_blood lives in ONE shared store and every organ writes the delta it produced on it, reconciled additively through the bigraph apply path (biological-modular-seam pattern). The shared pool drains more as more organs are added (monotone in N — a test asserts 8 organs drain it below the 2-organ case), which is only possible if the organs genuinely share the pool (contrast ensemble-and-multirate's N INDEPENDENT monoliths).

[scale] CRUCIAL caveat — accuracy and speed do NOT line up. The decomposed-vs-monolithic max_rel_err is a first-order additive-split error: 2e-3 at N=2, 1.2e-2 at N=8, 5.2e-2 at N=32, 0.31 (31%) at N=128. It HALVES as the coupling interval halves (verified) and GROWS with coupling density (more organs competing for the one pool per interval). The N=128 point where the end-to-end gap is smallest is exactly where accuracy (0.31) is unusable — so the speed crossover regime and the acceptable-accuracy regime do not co-occur at a fixed interval. Restoring accuracy at large N needs a finer interval, which adds more ticks and makes the decomposed run even slower. This is why the study verdict is PARTIAL.

[ABM limit] REDUCTION VALID AT LARGE N — at population scale K=400 (80 Gillespie-SSA runs, ~2 Lotka-Volterra periods, seed 0) the mean-field ODE integrated by libroadrunner/CVODE reproduces the SSA ensemble mean to a max relative error of 4.9% (mean 1.0%), with 0% predator extinction and 0% total extinction (robust across seeds: max rel err 0.033-0.056, extinction always 0). This is the Kurtz large-population limit in action: at enough individuals the discrete stochastic model and its continuous deterministic SBML reduction agree, so the ABM genuinely DOES reduce to an SBML model here.

[ABM limit] REDUCTION INVALID AT SMALL N — at scale K=8 (200 SSA runs, seed 0) the stochastic system COLLAPSES: the PREDATORS go extinct in 86.5% of runs and BOTH species in 51.0% (prey extinction, which is absorbing, then starves the predators), while the mean-field ODE — neutrally stable closed orbits — simply cycles forever and NEVER goes extinct (0% of either species, at any K). The ensemble mean diverges several-fold from the ODE (predator-extinct runs let the prey escape, so the mean bears no resemblance to the bounded ODE cycle). Robust across seeds (predator extinction 0.845-0.865, total 0.485-0.530). The deterministic SBML reduction misses the single most important qualitative behaviour of the small-population system — that the predators crash and the system can die out.

[ABM limit] HONEST EXTINCTION ACCOUNTING — only PREY extinction is truly absorbing; when the predators die but prey survive, the prey keep reproducing (pure birth r*X), so the SSA is NOT frozen on predator extinction (an earlier freeze inflated the single "extinction" number to 0.94 — the corrected, split numbers are 86.5% predator / 51.0% total). Prey that escape after their predators are gone are bounded by a documented population cap (25*K) that halts the unbounded runaway; the cap sits far above the deterministic orbit peak (~1.8 in density) so it never triggers while both species coexist. The headline metric is predator_extinct_fraction (the LV collapse the ODE can never show); total_extinct_fraction is reported alongside.

[ABM limit] STRUCTURAL LIMIT, NOT A TOLERANCE — the gap is not something a finer integrator or looser tolerance closes. The ODE state is (prey, predator) concentrations; it has no representation of integer discreteness, of demographic noise variance, or of the extinction probability, at ANY K. Those are properties of the ensemble and the absorbing boundary, which a single deterministic trajectory cannot carry. The ABM was NOT tuned to match the ODE — the large-N agreement and the small-N collapse are both measured.

[ABM limit] FEASIBILITY STATEMENT — "can an ABM even be an SBML/Tellurium model?" Answer: yes, but ONLY as its large-population, well-mixed, deterministic mean-field limit. That reduction is a real, runnable SBML model (the predator_prey_meanfield composite's Antimony) and is faithful when individuals are many; it silently discards stochasticity, discreteness, extinction and individual heterogeneity, which at small population size ARE the behaviour. This is the adversarial result that breaks the naive "just decompose/rewrite any model as SBML" claim the rest of the investigation operates under.

studies.claim: The one strong, well-measured result is that the MONOLITHIC libroadrunner BUILD strains superlinearly in the reaction count: 0.20 s at 97 species -> 1.76 s at 385 -> 5.54 s at 769 -> 18.5 s at 1537 species (~94x for ~16x the reactions, ~O(N^1.64)), with the dense-CVODE run blowing up alongside it (0.0023 s -> 2.56 s). That is the real strain point and the reason a very large SBML model is painful to run monolithically. Decomposition is NOT a free win: building N small models is SLOWER than the single compile up to ~100 species (1.7x slower at 97 species), reaches only rough parity at 385 species (1.40 vs 1.76 s) and becomes a clear build win only at ~1500 species (2.4x); and the decomposed per-tick RUN overhead is ~16x the monolith's CVODE run, so the decomposed body is SLOWER END-TO-END at every N measured (decomp_total 2.35 s vs mono_total 1.81 s at 385 species). The end-to-end gap narrows with N but the decomposed run is unmeasured past N=128, so no end-to-end crossover is claimed. Decomposition is a structural trade — it swaps the monolith's superlinear build for much higher run overhead — that would only pay off end-to-end on models larger than measured. CRUCIAL caveat: the additive-split accuracy is good only at small N / fine interval (max_rel_err 2e-3 at N=2, 1.2e-2 at N=8, 5.2e-2 at N=32) and is 0.31 (31%) at N=128 — so the regime where the speed gap narrows and the regime of acceptable accuracy do NOT co-occur at a fixed coupling interval. All numbers measured, not fabricated. ALSO: An agent-based model reduces to an SBML/Tellurium mean-field ODE ONLY in the large-population, well-mixed, deterministic limit; it structurally cannot capture stochasticity, discreteness, extinction, or individual heterogeneity. MEASURED (Lotka-Volterra, base rates r=a=b=m=1, start density (1.8, 1.0), horizon ~2 periods, seed 0): at a LARGE population scale K=400 (80 SSA runs) the mean-field ODE reproduces the SSA ensemble mean to a max relative error of 4.9% with 0% of runs seeing predator or total extinction — the reduction is VALID. At a SMALL scale K=8 (200 SSA runs) the stochastic system collapses: the PREDATORS go extinct in 86.5% of runs and BOTH species in 51.0%, hitting absorbing states that the neutrally-stable ODE — which simply orbits forever, 0% extinction of either species at any K — can never reach, and the ensemble mean diverges several-fold from the ODE (predator-extinct runs let the prey escape, so the mean no longer resembles the bounded ODE cycle). The ODE additionally cannot represent the ensemble variance at ANY K. So "can an ABM be an SBML model?" has an honest, quantified answer: yes, but only as its large-population mean-field limit, and that reduction silently discards exactly the stochastic/discrete phenomena (extinction, demographic noise) that are often the biological point. This breaks the naive "just write it as SBML" claim.

derived.insight: [scale] STRONG RESULT — the monolithic libroadrunner BUILD (compile) strains superlinearly: measured medians 0.20 s at 97 species, 1.76 s at 385, 5.54 s at 769, 18.5 s at 1537 species — ~94x the build cost for ~16x the reactions (~O(N^1.64)). The dense-CVODE integration blows up alongside it (0.0023 s -> 0.058 s -> 0.395 s -> 2.56 s). Both halves of the monolithic cost grow superlinearly; this is the real, well-measured strain point and this study's headline.
